body:
`NaturalCubicFitting` (#2378) has no tests in the suite. This adds three cases to `fittedbonddiscountcurve.cpp`:

- evaluation: with given parameters, the curve starts at 1, passes through the knots, matches `CubicNaturalSpline` between them and is flat after the last one; knots can be passed unsorted and with duplicates;
- knot validation: the errors for too few knots and for a negative knot time;
- calibration: a fit to ten annual bonds priced off a flat 3% curve stays within 1e-3 of that curve's discount factors and reprices the bonds within 0.05.

While writing them I found that a negative knot time was accepted. The constructor adds t = 0, sorts the knots and pins the discount factor at the first one to 1, so with knots `{-1, 1, 2}` the constraint moved to t = -1 and `d(0)` became a free parameter. The constructor now rejects negative knot times.

I also updated the class comment: it mentioned a `constrainAtZero` argument that the class does not have, and did not say that the curve is flat after the last knot.

The calibration tolerances leave room over what I measured (2.7e-4 and 0.011 at most over 450 evaluation dates between 2015 and 2030).

I used an AI assistant while preparing this and have reviewed and run all of it myself.
